speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng
text: asked the Minister for Health (a) since 2021, how many Singaporeans have successfully applied for MediFund at one healthcare institution and have at least an annual appointment at another healthcare institution (i) within the same cluster and (ii) in a different cluster respectively; (b) how many of such patients have successfully applied for MediFund across all healthcare clusters they have been to; and (c) whether the MediFund application process can be streamlined to support needy Singaporeans who cannot afford their healthcare bills across different healthcare institutions.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: This is to enable the Committees to exercise greater discretion in assessing MediFund applications and, thereby, improving their accessibility to these funds.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: However, this also inevitably leads to multiple assessments for the same patients across institutions: you transfer from acute hospital to community hospital, you go through one more round of assessment, and that adds to their inconvenience.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: We need to strike a balance between these two objectives of flexibility and convenience.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: This automatic support will be valid for a year from the time MediFund is first extended to him at the outpatient setting.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: Today, MediFund assistance is automatically extended to needy patients who are under ComCare assistance.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: MediFund assistance is withdrawn when the patients graduate from the ComCare scheme.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: I should clarify that under the law, MediFund Committees of each healthcare institution continue to have full discretion over the application outcome and extent of support, to prioritise support towards those who need it the most.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: Notwithstanding, MOH has been engaging them to agree to support the changes that I just mentioned.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: MOH will be issuing these guidelines to the MediFund Committees.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: These enhancements should help smoothen the experience for MediFund beneficiaries as they transfer or seek care in different healthcare settings, and we expect them to come into force by March 2024.

speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng (Jurong)
text: I declare that I am a medical doctor at a public healthcare institution.

speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng (Jurong)
text: Eleven years ago, a number of young healthcare workers, including myself and others, had advocated for such improvements within the same healthcare institution campus.

speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng (Jurong)
text: In 2016, seven years ago, I had asked a Parliamentary Question on how we could smoothen that journey across different hospitals across Singapore.

speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng (Jurong)
text: These are welcome developments, and I would like to ask the Minister two supplementary questions.

speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng (Jurong)
text: A less-mobile resident who needs a caregiver to accompany, this has implications for the caregiver, too.

speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng (Jurong)
text: Can I ask the Minister, are there ways we can better resource our medical social worker (MSW) departments so that more patients can have the assessment and review with an MSW on the same day that they come to the clinic or for treatment at the hospital?

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: But I thank the Member for the persistence and I know Dr Tan Wu Meng has been knocking on this door for a long time.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: Like all policies, it takes time for us to look at it and find ways to implement it in a way that everyone can accept.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: So, I think persistence does pay off and I know Dr Tan has also been equally persistent in asking for the elderly who are immobile, in terms of the portability of their subsidy as well of their MediFund eligibility.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: One way is to go digital and make things easier, but that also introduces its own impediments.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: But it will be a useful channel for the immobile or home-bound patients to also apply for medical and financial assistance.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: The other is that we have now implemented Healthier SG and also Age Well SG with a whole network of active ageing centres (AACs) throughout our communities.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: We want to double the number, expand the network, deepen the kind of help they can extend to our aged residents.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: So, they can also be a channel from which I would not rule out that, in time to come, they can also be a channel for us to guide our aged and seniors to apply for assistance there.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: So, keep on putting forward such suggestions to us.
